notes: Correct and robust, including refreshing the run when the parent is unchanged, but it loads all attempt jobs per caller, adds more machinery than needed, and returns an error from cancelRun after the transaction has already committed; the tests are thorough and realistic.

Works and also repairs already-stuck runs by refreshing the run when the parent is unchanged, but the caller path is convoluted (refresh, then a full-attempt descendant scan, then possibly overwriting) and it returns an emit error after the transaction has committed.

Making cancelOneJob aggregate expanded callers from their children is order-independent and handles any nesting depth, and the settle path emits correctly; it relies on IsExpanded implying children exist and leaves a now-stale comment, but its nested StopTask test and mocked emit test are strong.

Expanded callers are re-aggregated from their children inside cancelOneJob, and the emitter is triggered only when the settle path actually ran; the fix relies on the IsExpanded flag rather than on children being present, and its nested-caller and emit tests are solid.

Correctly re-aggregates expanded callers (nested and top-level) from their children instead of overwriting them as Cancelled, and emits after a settle-only cancel like the reference; however the refresh block is duplicated, and the only test change rewrites the existing force-cancel test, adding no nested-depth or emit test.
Equivalent to the reference in logic, with somewhat duplicated caller-refresh blocks; its only test change rewrites an existing force-cancel subtest instead of adding nested or emit coverage.

Only the top-level caller is refreshed, so nested callers are still written Cancelled over a cancelling grandchild (the 'any nesting depth' requirement fails), it double-emits on every cancel, its test covers only a single level, and it fails the hidden tests.

Only the top-level caller is re-aggregated, so nested callers are still written Cancelled while a child is cancelling; it also emits unconditionally and duplicates the existing emit, and it fails the hidden tests.

A clean helper refreshes expanded callers that have children (checking both IsExpanded and child count), closely mirroring the reference, and its services test verifies the waiter actually wakes; minor issues are a redundant emit when jobs were also updated and an unrelated comment move in TestSettleRunAfterCancel.

Closely mirrors the reference by refreshing expanded callers that have children instead of force-writing Cancelled; it may emit twice when jobs were updated, makes an unrelated comment move in an existing test, and has a strong concurrency-wake test.

Keeping a caller cancelling while any direct child is cancelling works through the cascade at any depth, but it always returns or appends the caller even when unchanged, discards the error from EmitJobsIfReadyByRun (errcheck), emits even when the run did not change, and adds no services test.

This is a minimal and correct check that a cancelling child keeps the caller cancelling, and it handles nesting, but it silently discards the error from EmitJobsIfReadyByRun (an errcheck violation) and adds no test for the emit path.

Fixes both problems and defensively makes UpdateRunJob always refresh the run, but that causes a redundant double refresh whenever the parent changes; it also unconditionally rewrites callers and replaces EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs with an unconditional run emit, a wider change than needed.

Correctly keeps callers cancelling while a child is cancelling, but it also changes the UpdateRunJob hot path to refresh the run on every child update, even when the parent cascade already did, and always emits per run; it has no nested test.

Callers with children are re-read and re-aggregated instead of overwritten, which fixes nested depth, but the caller is always appended even when unchanged, and the targeted EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs is replaced by an unconditional run emit; good nested and services tests.

A caller with children is re-read and re-aggregated in cancelOneJob, which works, but it always returns the caller even when nothing changed and replaces EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs with an unconditional per-run emit on every cancel.

Functionally correct and also refreshes the run when the parent caller is unchanged, but it loads every attempt job per caller, redundantly overrides the refresh result, and returns an emit error after the transaction has already committed.

Adds a sensible UpdateRunJob fallback when the parent is unchanged, but its cancelOneJob caller logic is redundant (refresh plus a full-attempt descendant scan for every caller), and it returns an error after the commit if the emit fails; tests are thorough, including the stuck-state recovery.

A clean fix inside cancelOneJob: expanded callers aggregate from their children regardless of processing order, and the force-cancel emit uses a correct settled flag; it relies on IsExpanded rather than actual children, and the tests cover the nested acknowledgement and the emit.

Re-aggregates expanded callers inside cancelOneJob, which works for nested callers regardless of processing order, and emits by run after a settle-only cancel; it has no guard for an expanded caller with zero children, and the nested test's IDs break the parent<child invariant.

Fixes the bug at every nesting level by re-aggregating expanded callers from their children, and the emit condition is correct; however, the refresh runs on stale structs, the same block is duplicated, and the only test change rewrites the existing force-cancel subtest, losing its original scenario, with no acknowledgement or emit test.

Refreshes descendant and top callers that have children, and its emit condition closely matches the reference; the refresh block is duplicated, and it repurposes an existing force-cancel test instead of adding nested or emission tests.

Only the top-level caller is re-aggregated, so nested callers are still written Cancelled directly ahead of a cancelling child, breaking the 'any nesting depth' requirement; it also double-emits and fails the hidden tests.

Only fixes the top-level caller, so nested descendant callers are still overwritten to Cancelled and stay stuck; it also always double-emits, fails the hidden tests, and adds only a single-level test.

A sound helper refreshes expanded callers that have children at each level, with good nested and concurrency-waiter tests; however, the emit can fire redundantly when jobs were updated, and it moves a comment in an unrelated existing test.

Refreshes expanded callers that have children from those children and falls back to a direct cancel for unexpanded or childless callers; emission when the run is done can duplicate the per-job emit, there is an unrelated test-comment move, and the tests are strong (nested chain plus a real concurrency waiter).

Works by keeping a caller cancelling only when a direct child is Cancelling, relying on the cascade to heal ordering; the service change ignores EmitJobsIfReadyByRun's error, emits even when nothing changed, and has no service test.

A minimal check keeps a caller with a Cancelling direct child unchanged and the nested test passes, but it silently ignores EmitJobsIfReadyByRun's error, emits even when the run did not change, and has no service-level test.

Correct, and it additionally heals already-stuck runs by always refreshing the run in UpdateRunJob, but that adds redundant run refreshes on every child update; it also swaps EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs for an unconditional per-run emit, while the tests are good, including a stuck-state case.

Works, but makes UpdateRunJob refresh the run on every child update, a redundant double refresh on a hot path; it sets the caller from a direct-child Cancelling check instead of aggregating, swaps the emit to an unconditional per-run emit, and tests only one nesting level.

A clean fix: callers with children are re-read and re-aggregated instead of written Cancelled, and a per-run emit releases blocked concurrency runs; it always returns the caller even when unchanged, and the tests cover the nested acknowledgement and the emit.
Correctly re-reads and re-aggregates callers that have children, but always returns the caller even when unchanged and replaces the targeted EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs with an unconditional per-run emit.
